title: Chamber size by largest connected pipe
statement: The chamber size of a manhole follows the largest connected pipe diameter D: D below 375 mm → DN1200; between 375 and 700 mm → DN1500; between 700 and 900 mm → DN1800; above 900 mm → 'Consult Undertaker'.
inputs: pipe diameters P0–P4 of the connections in use

evidence.detail: cond with strict < and > comparisons; attribute CS

Extracted cond run in VeLisp 0.8.0: 0.375, 0.700, 0.900 m return nil (no band); 0.300, 0.450, 1.000 m return DN1200, DN1500, Consult Undertaker. Supports the suspected defect for the extracted logic; the original routine in AutoCAD is not yet observed.

authority.basis: 'Consult Undertaker' points to the sewerage undertaker's adoption requirements; table not cited

legacy_defect.description: Diameters of exactly 375, 700 or 900 mm match no band, so the CS attribute is left unchanged (keeps any previous value). 375 mm is a common pipe size.

required_human_ruling: Which band do 375, 700 and 900 mm belong to?

title: Depth to soffit
statement: Depth to soffit is the cover level minus the highest pipe soffit, where each soffit is the invert level plus the pipe diameter, over the connections in use (1 to 4, from the block's visibility state). The result is written to attribute SOFFIT to 3 decimals.
dependencies: get_block_att (two different definitions in 0 - Function library.lsp; the later one wins)

evidence.detail: top_i = IL_i + P_i; DTS = CL - max(top_i)

authority.basis: depth to soffit is a standard manhole schedule quantity

uncertainty: Visibility state '0' and '1' both use connections 0 and 1

title: Manhole type by depth to soffit
statement: Manhole type follows depth to soffit d: 3 ≤ d ≤ 6 → type A; 1.5 ≤ d ≤ 3 → B; 1 ≤ d ≤ 1.5 → E; below 1 or above 6 → CHECK.

evidence.detail: cond; boundaries 3 and 1.5 belong to two bands and are decided by evaluation order

authority.basis: type letters match adoption-standard manhole types; not cited

uncertainty: d = 3 gives A and d = 1.5 gives B only because of the order of the tests
required_human_ruling: Confirm the boundary assignments at 1.5 m and 3 m

title: Pipe diameter read from attribute text
statement: Pipe diameters are read from attributes P0–P4 by taking characters 3 to 7 of the text (format 'DN' followed by millimetres) and converting to metres.
uncertainty: Any other text format (e.g. 'Ø375', '375mm') reads as 0 without warning
required_human_ruling: In a new platform, store diameter as a number, not text
